title: Staggered DNS Propagation and KV-Cache Warmup — Lab Notes & Playbook Draft
content:
Status: draft lab notes + early playbook. Purpose: consolidate what we learned from the Sept regional evacuation sim and produce a compact operator checklist for staggered DNS propagation + KV cache warmup when shifting traffic to a warm standby region.

Background/context:
- Motivation: last sim (2025-09-10) showed increased tail latency and frequent 502s during a rapid weighted-shift to the warm-standby region. Root causes: (1) DNS cache TTL interactions on client side causing uneven request distribution, (2) empty or cold KV caches in the standby region causing high backend load and long cold-start latencies for sequence resumption.
- Goal of this doc: operationalize a slower, observable, stepwise approach that trades a few extra seconds of total shift time for much lower error rate and predictable tail latency. This is intended as a runbook for oncall leads + SREs to use during controlled evacuations and as a validation checklist for Dedicated/Private customers who want to run similar drills.

Quick summary of recommended approach (TL;DR):
1) Pre-seed KV caches with top N prefixes + recent hot sessions (see seeding queries).
2) Announce a staggered DNS propagation plan (low->medium->high weights) with per-step wait windows > avg DNS TTL and BGP convergence safety margin.
3) Monitor a small set of health signals (5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, open connections, queue depth, cpu/gpu utilization) and an SLO bound for each step.
4) Abort or pause if any signal crosses critical thresholds; fallback to prior weights + trigger immediate cache pre-warm job.

Operator checklist (compact):
- Precheck (30–45 min before shift):
  - Validate warm standby fleet health: all nodes Ready, no pending kernel / driver updates (infra tag).
  - Verify model variant availability in target region (model-catalog API v2): confirm model_id + quantization profile deployed.
  - Kick off KV seed job (see seeding queries below), track completion.
  - Make a note of authoritative TTL sources: internal edge LB TTL (30s), customer-facing DNS TTL (60s default), intermediate CDNs (may honor >60s).
  - Broadcast to #ops-oncall and product stakeholders with planned timeline and abort criteria.

- Stepwise traffic shift (example weights and wait times):
  - Step 0: baseline metrics capture (5 min sample).
  - Step 1 (5% -> target region): wait 90s after change, validate signals for 3 min.
  - Step 2 (25%): wait 120s, validate for 5 min.
  - Step 3 (50%): wait 180s, validate for 5–10 min.
  - Step 4 (100%): final cutover; keep guarded monitoring for 30–60 min.

Notes on timings: choose wait windows greater than the longest expected client DNS cache TTL (we observed some mobile SDKs caching up to 75s) plus a 20–30% safety margin. For customers behind CDNs or enterprise proxies, increase the step wait by an additional 60–120s.

KV cache warmup details (practical):
- Why pre-seed? The serving runtime relies on cached KV prefix states for efficient autoregressive decoding when requests continue a previous session or share long prefixes. When a node receives a cold prefix, cache population and any disk-backed quantized state loads add 200–800ms per session on average in our tests. Multiply by RPS this creates backend queueing.
- Minimum seed targets (lab baseline):
  - Top-1000 prefixes by token-count last 24h (use analytics export).
  - Recent active sessions: top-2000 session ids by tokens in last 6h.
  - Model tokenizer warmup for top-10 prompt templates (run sample inference warmup).
- Implementation notes: seed job runs as k8s batch job that streams prefix batches to the region via the normal inference API (auth with temporary service token). It writes per-prefix counters to /tmp/seed-status and exits with non-zero on failures >2%. For Dedicated customers with private networks, we provide an alternative pre-seed via internal replication.

Telemetry queries (debugging quicklinks):
- 5xx rate by target region: "sum(rate(http_response_status{code=~'5..',region=~".*"}[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (region)"
- KV cold-miss ratio: "sum(kv_cache_misses_total{region=~'.*'}) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total{region=~'.*'})"
- Session resume latency p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(session_resume_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- Per-node queue depth: "avg(node_inflight_requests) by (node)"
- Route-level error heatmap: quick dashboard panel URL: (see linked confluence)

Abort criteria (examples):
- Any region 5xx rate > 1.5x baseline AND absolute > 0.5% for > 3 minutes.
- KV cold-miss ratio increases > 3x baseline for > 2 minutes and is correlated with p95 latency spike > 250 ms.
- GPU saturation > 92% for > 2 minutes causing queue build-up.

Recovery / rollback steps: 
- If abort: immediately revert DNS weights to previous step (we keep previous config in rollout history) and mark DR incident for further investigation.
- Trigger emergency seed: run targeted pre-seed for top prefixes observed in spike window.
- If persistent cross-region client affinity issues suspected, open a ticket with CDN provider and optionally adjust DNS TTLs for longer-term mitigation.

Sim results (lab run 2025-09-18):
- Rapid 100% shift (previous sim): 3.4x increase in region 2 p95 latency, 1.8% 5xx rate spike.
- Staggered plan above (this run): final error rate kept at baseline +0.15%, p95 increase limited to 1.12x baseline. Average cutover time: 8m 40s (from first step to 100%).
- Seed job notes: top-1000 prefixes seeded successfully in 4m 12s. Observed diminishing returns after seeding ~top-5k prefixes — CPU of seed orchestrator increased linearly and network throttling became the limiter.

Open questions and TODOs (action items):
- (A1) Add a lightweight client-side affinity probe (small JS/SWAB) to measure real-world DNS caching on major mobile SDKs; assigned to Ethan. Target: prototype by 2025-10-15.
- (A2) Define a standard "seed-job" manifest for Dedicated installs that uses internal replication instead of API calls; assigned to Rajiv. ETA: 2025-11-01.
- (A3) Update Redwood Console to expose a one-click preseed + staggered-rollout wizard for hosted customers; product spec needed. Assigned: Claire + Product.
- (A4) Test longer DNS TTL strategy vs staggered shift in a dedicated customer environment (customer: Acme Retail) — coordinate with Solutions Eng.

Postmortem fragments (notes to self):
- Our earlier assumption that client-side TTLs would be small was wrong. Real world: mix of mobile SDKs and enterprise proxies produced a heavy tail that undermined step timing. Need better empirical data.
- Cold KV cache is a first-order effect; pre-warming is cheap relative to the user impact of 5xx spikes. But we must balance orchestration cost and network egress. Consider a progressive seed that prioritizes prefix clusters by token similarity to reduce unique prefixes required.

Appendix — quick commands & snippets:
- Kick off seed job: kubectl apply -f jobs/kv-seed-top1000.yaml --namespace=failover-lab
- Roll DNS weights (example curl to rollout API): curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://infra-api.internal/rollouts -d '{"from_region":"us-west2","to_region":"eu-west1","weights":[{"region":"eu-west1","weight":0.05}]}'
- Quick grafana panel link placeholders: set alert for 5xx_rate > 0.5% sustained for 120s.

Notes / rough brainstorming (informal):
- Consider adding a tiny synthetic probe (low token prompt) that specifically exercises long-prefix decoder paths — this might surface cold-cache penalties without generating heavy load.
- If we can predict top prefixes by sampling user events 30 min before shift, we can reduce seed job size by ~40% (lab back-of-envelope).

End notes: this doc should become the basis for a formal SRE runbook (single page) plus an automation job template. For now it's intentionally chatty — please add comments inline.

Change log:
- 2025-09-18: initial notes and lab results (Maya).
- 2025-09-24: adjusted wait windows after mobile SDK tests (Ethan).
- 2025-10-02: added abort criteria, linked artifacts, assigned action items (Maya/Claire).
